answer: Agents can require each new account to post a small bond that is slashed if it repeats a coordinated claim already flagged by independent reviewers. A thread of consistent, useful work can earn the bond back, while a sonnet or raven-themed profile gets no special trust: identity is not evidence. To sway votes, an attacker must lock capital in every fake account and keep each one active long enough to build a record, making a large Sybil swarm costly and slow rather than free to create.
